about: What tools/build_latest.ps1 builds: the newest playable state. The orchestrator keeps this current as branches land; every listed merge is checked to be conflict-free when it changes. Branch names are without origin/; paths are relative to unity/.
contents: The farmland preview at physics model 104, on the Play build (Play opens two maps, House and Village; M opens the world's map). New since the model 103 build: the spool's pull is drawn light on every flight (model 104), so an ordinary turn-around no longer puts the line into a prop because of a heavy spool, and a break is judged only on a tension the physics really applied; and the menu is Play, Calibrate and Exit, with Explore and the small describing labels gone (D-117). Since the model 100 build: the physics steps are faster where they froze or crawled (the laid fiber's checks against a ruin's many boxes, and the wind's sheltering map rebuilt on four threads instead of one), with every result unchanged; a drone's parts no longer pass through a wire's cable at speed (model 101); the fiber no longer breaks where it wraps thin boards and slabs, as in the ruins, and wood, bark and fabric wear it only mildly (model 102); the ruins' walls are solid between their two drawn faces, the stove and chimney half-brick shells (model 103); and the game is built on IL2CPP instead of Mono (D-116): its physics step runs about 1.6 to 1.8 times faster at the median, the 0.15 to 0.23 s stall at the start of every flight is gone, and every flight still replays bit for bit on the test tools. New since model 85. Straw, tall grass and tree crowns act on the props: a blade cuts a stem only where it is fast enough, each cut takes work from the rotor and pushes its arm, and the summary names what each rotor cut (how many stems, of what, for how many joules); a drone in a crown falls through the twigs with the props turning and cutting, and rests only on a branch or the ground. The legs are the hand-made ones: each of the four has its own stiffness, drawn from the flight's seed and written in the log; a leg cracks, sets, kinks, folds and tears by its tube's own law, and a broken half hangs from its neighbour and lies on the ground instead of in it. The contact bug that tumbled cut landings on 10 to 20 degree slopes is fixed (a foot's hold stretched by metres). A fast prop meets a thin branch or a wire instead of passing through it. The wind takes the farmland's groves, hedges and thin ruin walls for what they are, and its gusts scale with height: near the ground they are smaller and quicker, as the air's are there (model 100). The drone's own rotor wake shakes it at its measured level (at most 6.2 % of the hover's thrust either way, less in cruise), and a descent through its own wash moves the thrust both ways. The fiber turns at the canister's exit as on a point, a resting line is held instead of thrown, the rotors' wash reaches the ground from any height, and the line lying under the drone moves in it. Everything else is as in the Play build: Village's hills, trees, bushes and ruins solid, the wind over the hills, the friend's look, the analog feed, the OSD, the motors, the failsafe, R, C, X, V, pause, the summary and the flight log. Known, being fixed after the pilot's flights on model 103 (D-117, D-118): the drone still stands on two rails, and wet ground still holds it like a magnet, lets it slide and then jump (four separate legs like the pilot's kit, digging into the soil, are being built); a landing still slides and rocks too lightly; the OSD is still laid over the analog picture instead of going through the channel with it; over a ruin the laid fiber can lie straight through walls and beams, and in Severe wind it slides off roofs; a full-stick turn-around can still put the line into the front-left prop on some spool draws; the plants do not push the drone yet (built as model 105, held back until its cost in dense weeds is cut), and the drawn grass and trees do not move in the flight's wind yet; the two wire whiskers on the nose are not drawn, and the props in the frame are still the still ones (the turning props go in with the camera where it is). Known, not judged yet: a leg cracks from 0.3 m/s of sideways drift at touchdown and most break or bend at 0.6 m/s, and on a kerb the damage jumps from none at 1.25 m/s to three or four legs at 1.5 m/s; a conductor met at the frame now stops the drone hard (the clamp's own failure and the wire's give are not modelled). Known: a very sharp liftoff or a low move back over the laid line does not cut the fiber on the props yet; the fiber can still slip through a 2 mm twig late in a long wrap; the physics step is still over its budget in the game where the laid line lies on a ruin's many shapes; the hull's turning moment in a crosswind is measured but not flown; straw under the drone folds by the plain column of air (the wash with distance is built for it and switched off); on House a landing on a trench's soil can sink in; the frame rate was measured on the Play build and not again on this one (111 fps through the feed in the laptop's Performance mode, about 60 in Quiet mode); the fiber's dragged corner at a sharp low turn was not measured again; our trenches, houses and cars are not in Village yet (W5, half built); the open map covers the OSD's centre; on House's map the houses are only about 10 px across; a pine's thick arms are needle cards and still flutter; on Calibrate's Rates tab the minus and plus buttons draw blank.
